design: Display only. Nothing new is recorded: tasks.spec_document_id is set when a document materialises its tasks and, for an agent's create_task, when its requirement_ids resolve to one document (hub/hub/api/v1/tasks.py:821). Since 2026-10-24 the review briefing tells a reviewer to name requirement_ids and spec_document on a side finding (hub/hub/review_turn.py findings_lines), so follow-ups from reviews now carry the document. A task counts as open when its status is anything other than approved or rejected. A follow-up is a task whose spec_task_key is empty or is not among the document's declared task keys.

checked: On :8000 (read-only), project proj-d85a82bf4216: slice 2's 7 declared tasks are approved; 5 follow-ups filed by QA during review; 1 of them (task-6ac1bb3d4d39) carries spdoc-75175af77f8f, the other 4 named no requirements and carry none; none carries the flow's loop_id
Only DependencyListView.tsx groups tasks by document; TaskCardCompact.tsx and TaskDetailDrawer.tsx don't name it
A roadmap slice's state is the phase of the document naming it (a-roadmap-shows-which-of-its-slices-are-done), so an approved document reads as done regardless of its open tasks
limits: Whether the tasks route's spec_document_id filter returns follow-ups and declared tasks in one call was not driven
The acceptance criteria are proposed coverage; none has been run

problem: Operator, 2026-10-24: "It's hard to know from which spec each task came", and slice 2 of the red thread (spdoc-75175af77f8f) looked finished while five follow-ups were open, three of them defects it had introduced. Every task already records its document (tasks.spec_document_id, set by the document's materialisation or by the requirements an agent names), but only the Dependencies view groups tasks by document. Board cards and the task drawer don't name it. A document's flow lists only its own queue (loop_id), so a follow-up filed with create_task appears nowhere near the document. The flow stopped when its queue emptied, and nothing on the document or its roadmap slice said that work against it was still open.

requirements.rationale: The operator could not find which spec a task came from. Showing 'No spec' rather than nothing tells apart 'none' from 'not loaded'.
requirements.statement: Every task card on the board names the title of the specification document the task belongs to; a task that belongs to no document is marked 'No spec' instead.

requirements.rationale: The drawer is where someone reads one task's whole story; the document is the standard it was built against.
requirements.statement: A task's drawer names its document's title and phase, with a control that opens that document; a task with no document says it belongs to none.

requirements.rationale: A follow-up a reviewer filed during the flow carries the document but not the flow's queue, so the flow's own list never shows it.
requirements.statement: A specification document's page lists every task whose document is that document, each with its title, status and assignee, and marks the tasks the document did not declare as follow-ups.

requirements.rationale: Slice 2 read as done (approved, flow stopped) with five tasks open. The count is a warning, not a gate (operator, 2026-10-08: approvals are scarce, warn don't gate).
requirements.statement: An approved change document whose tasks are not all approved or rejected shows how many are still open, on its page header and beside its slice on its roadmap's page; with none open, nothing extra is shown.

in_scope: The document a task belongs to, named on its board card and in its drawer, with a way to open it
A plain 'no spec' marking on a task that belongs to no document
A document's page listing every task against it, its declared tasks and its follow-ups alike, with each one's status
A count of open tasks on an approved change document, and beside its slice on the roadmap page
non_goals: Per-spec statistics: cost, run counts, evidence verdicts per runner, time per task (vault note src-109565ec0558; a separate change)
Adding follow-up tasks to a flow's queue automatically, or restarting a stopped flow
Changing how a slice's phase is derived, or blocking approval or archive on open tasks
Guessing a document for a task whose requirements name none or several (the Hub records nothing then, deliberately)
Changing the reviewer's instructions (done separately as a Tier 0 change on 2026-10-24)

summary: Every task names the specification document it belongs to, on the board and in its drawer, and says so plainly when it belongs to none. A document's page lists every task against it, including follow-ups a reviewer filed during its flow, so a document whose flow has stopped no longer looks finished while work against it is still open.

tasks.description: Name the document's title on each board card (or 'No spec') and its title, phase and an open control in the task drawer. The task payload already carries spec_document_id; resolve titles from the project's documents. UI tests with fixtures in the order the routes return them; mock first (hub/ui/mock), then wire; refresh the committed UI bundle.
tasks.title: Board card and drawer name the task's spec

tasks.description: On a document's page, list every task with that spec_document_id (the tasks route already filters by it), marking those whose spec_task_key the document does not declare as follow-ups; show the open count on the header and beside the slice on the roadmap page. Write the acceptance drive (ac-drive) first and record it failing.
tasks.title: A document lists its tasks and shows what is open

title: A task shows the spec it came from, and a spec shows its open follow-ups
